claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has coarse dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Internal boundaries in the coarse lamellar colonies promote microcrack initiation during tensile deformation.
Severe plastic deformation will refine the lamellar spacing.
Severe plastic deformation will increase dislocation density.
Minimal thermal exposure during processing will help avoid unwanted recrystallization.
Refined lamellar spacing and increased dislocation density along phase boundaries will produce a more homogeneous stress distribution.
Reducing the width of coarse lamellar colonies will lower stress concentrations at internal boundaries.
The relevant internal boundaries are sites where microcracks typically initiate.
Increased dislocation density will enhance strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening will contribute to improved tensile strength.
Enhanced strain hardening will contribute to improved tensile ductility.
SPD-treated alloys will have higher tensile strength than the untreated baseline.
SPD-treated alloys will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the untreated baseline.
SPD-treated alloys will develop fewer microcracks during deformation than the untreated baseline.
The untreated alloy's internal boundaries act as microcrack nucleation sites, causing low room-temperature tensile ductility and eventual catastrophic failure.
The intervention is expected to be effective in eutectic high-entropy alloys having similar dual-phase lamellar structures.
Processing temperatures that cause coarsening may limit the intervention's effectiveness.
